review::.::holistic::cross_module_archit.summary: The Workspace generation_lock publication protocol is honored by the LSP transport only; daemon dispatchers query and mutate without it

evidence: crates/al-workspace/src/lib.rs:152-158 documents generation_lock as the workspace-wide publication contract: "LSP request handlers hold a read guard while querying; a reindex holds the write guard only for the final in-memory swap."

Every acquisition of generation_lock in the repository is in crates/al-lsp/src/server/{lsp.rs,workspace.rs,diagnostics.rs}. No file under crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/ acquires it, in either direction.

crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/build_dispatch/build/file_refresh.rs:156-174 and :261-278 publish in-memory mutations (documents.replace_or_open / rename, file_index.add_file / remove_file, invalidate_insight_graph) and bump the revision via mark_generation_changed, but never take the write guard, while crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/mod.rs serves up to MAX_CONNECTIONS = 64 concurrent requests.

The daemon substitutes an unrelated protocol — project_state_with_wait at crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/mod.rs:1002-1031 wraps a 500ms LOCK_WAIT timeout in block_in_place/block_on and returns "Project state is busy (configuration reload or reindex in progress); retry the request".

The same query is reached both ways with different readiness discipline: crates/al-lsp/src/server/lsp.rs:1606-1624 (hover) calls snapshot_after_ready, ensure_builtins_loaded and re-checks snapshot_is_current, while dispatch_hover in crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/lsp_dispatch.rs does only ensure_document before calling the same al_analysis::queries::hover::hover_full.
detail.suggestion: Move the guard into al-workspace so it cannot be transport-specific: wrap the file_refresh mutations in a `Workspace::publish_generation(|| ...)` helper that takes the write guard and bumps the revision in one place, and have the daemon's query dispatchers take the read guard the same way the LSP handlers do. review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: al-explorer pins edition 2024 while all 20 sibling crates inherit 2021, creating a formatting and semantics island

evidence: crates/al-explorer/Cargo.toml line 4 is `edition = "2024"`. Every other crate manifest says `edition.workspace = true`, and [workspace.package] in the root Cargo.toml sets edition = "2021". No comment in the manifest explains the pin.

Rustfmt's style edition follows the crate edition, so the pin changes use-tree sorting. al-explorer: `use crate::{App, MAX_INPUT_LEN, advance_list_selection, ensure_daemon_client, input_focused_style};` (views/call_graph.rs:12) and `use crate::{ActivePane, App, ClickTarget, MAX_INPUT_LEN, display_object_id, pad_center, pane_style, truncate_with_ellipsis};` (views/object_browser.rs:10) put uppercase items before lowercase ones.

Everywhere else the ordering is the opposite: `use al_protocol::jsonrpc::{error_codes, Response};`, `use al_syntax::context::{detect_context, CompletionContext};`, `use crate::queries::tests::{collect_test_procedures, TestCodeunit};`, `pub use lsp::{run_lsp, AlServer};`. A grep for the uppercase-first ordering across al-analysis, al-lsp and al-symbols returned zero matches, so the split is exactly at the al-explorer boundary.

The edition also changes language semantics for this one crate (match ergonomics, unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn, tail-expression temporary drop scope), so an idiom copied from a sibling crate can behave differently here — relevant given crates/al-explorer/src/main.rs already contains an `unsafe` libc::signal block.
detail.suggestion: Either change crates/al-explorer/Cargo.toml to `edition.workspace = true` and run `cargo fmt -p al-explorer` to bring its imports back in line, or, if edition 2024 is deliberate (for example to pick up a specific ratatui/crossterm idiom), record the reason in a comment above the key and add `style_edition = "2024"` to a workspace rustfmt.toml so the whole workspace formats the same way. review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: Most al-explorer CLI commands hand-roll the connect/request/format block the documented run_command helper exists for

evidence: commands/mod.rs:376 defines run_command and :395 run_command_with_exit, documented as the standard path, with the exception spelled out: "Commands with conditional exit codes, multi-step logic, early returns inside the format branch, or non-standard timeouts should stay manual".
Across cli/commands/*.rs and cli/commands/lsp/*.rs there are about 63 hand-rolled `match connect(...)` blocks against about 25 run_command call sites.
Two whole modules never use it: lsp/env.rs (6 cmd_ functions) and lsp/language.rs (8 cmd_ functions).

The exception does not explain all of them. cmd_position_query (lsp/language.rs:316) and cmd_generate (lsp/reports.rs:7) each do exactly connect -> request_checked -> if json print_json else format -> ExitCode::SUCCESS, which is run_command's shape verbatim.

Each hand-rolled copy repeats the `match connect(None) { Ok(c) => c, Err(e) => return report_error(&e, json) }` prologue, so the error-reporting behaviour of a command depends on which copy its author started from.
detail.suggestion: Convert the commands whose bodies match the helper's shape — starting with cmd_position_query, cmd_symbols/cmd_folding/cmd_tokens, cmd_generate and the rest of lsp/reports.rs — to run_command or run_command_with_exit. Leave the genuinely non-standard ones (cmd_daemon_shutdown, cmd_setup, cmd_doctor, cmd_format's stdin/check paths) manual, and add a one-line comment on each naming which exception applies.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: 26-field `Workspace` god-struct is threaded into 145 al-analysis query signatures that use three of its fields

evidence: al-workspace/src/lib.rs:143 `pub struct Workspace` declares 26 fields (20 public) covering DocumentStore, SymbolIndex, toolchain, AlProject, the .NET semantic bridge, merged AlConfig, builtins, compiler error codes, a native debug session, profiler session, test results, four lazily-built graph caches and six lock/counter primitives.

Counting field accesses across al-analysis: file_index 145, documents 94, symbols 91, get_or_build_call_graph 12, profiler_session 10, config 7, generation_revision 3, test_results 2, builtins 2 — roughly 10 of the 26 members are ever reached, and three account for the bulk.

Consequence: `queries::definition::definition(&Workspace, uri, pos)` is handed the live debug session and profiler state, so a reader cannot tell from a signature what state a query depends on, and a query cannot be exercised without constructing the whole server.
detail.suggestion: Introduce a narrow read-side view — e.g. `pub struct SourceSnapshot<'a> { documents: &'a DocumentStore, symbols: &'a SymbolIndex, file_index: &'a FileIndex }` in al-workspace, with `Workspace::snapshot(&self) -> SourceSnapshot<'_>` — and change the al-analysis query signatures to take it. The handful of queries that genuinely need more (code_lens reads profiler_session, impact reads the call graph) keep `&Workspace`, which then documents itself as the exception. This removes a parameter's worth of reach rather than adding a layer: no new trait, no new crate, one struct.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: 1451-line hand-maintained runtime schema validator compensates for the missing typed response structs, and covers only 60 of 84 daemon methods

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.summary: Workspace bootstrap is implemented twice, in al-workspace and again in al-lsp, with divergent async bridging and staging

evidence: al_workspace::initialize_core_workspace (lib.rs:789) runs find_project -> apply_symbol_settings -> load_packages_cached_lenient -> load_runtime_enums -> replace_package_info -> file_index.scan -> find_toolchain; it is called by the daemon (daemon/mod.rs:1200) and the test harness.
al-lsp's initialize_workspace (server/workspace.rs:66, ~415 lines) runs the same sequence again inline, with its own set_package_info helper at line 752.
The two bridge sync filesystem work differently: the core version uses tokio::task::block_in_place (with a comment explaining the &Workspace borrow), the LSP version uses spawn_blocking.

Only the LSP version stages into a fresh FileIndex/SymbolIndex and publishes a generation (publish_complete_generation, line 517); the daemon path scans in place, so the two entry points give different atomicity guarantees for the same operation.
The LSP version also interleaves client.show_message calls with every staging step, so the transport concern and the state-staging concern cannot be reused independently.
detail.suggestion: Make initialize_core_workspace the single staged implementation: have it return the staged FileIndex/SymbolIndex plus a CoreInitResult and take a `&dyn Fn(Severity, String)` progress sink instead of speaking to a client. al-lsp's initialize_workspace then becomes the LSP-specific wrapper that supplies a sink calling client.show_message, adds the cancellation checks and the download prompt, and calls publish_complete_generation. The daemon keeps its current call unchanged and gains the staged semantics.

The path-escape check stays in the dispatcher (it is a transport-trust concern), the routing, event pump and coverage merge move down.

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.summary: The dispatch layer maps 194 error paths to INTERNAL_ERROR, discarding al-analysis's typed error taxonomy

evidence: al-analysis query signatures carry ~14 distinct error enums (WorkspaceQueryError, TestQueryError, AuditError, SourceLookupError, ImpactError, ProfilerHintError, ...) alongside 50 Result<_, String>.
Across the daemon dispatch layer error_codes::INTERNAL_ERROR is used 194 times against 12 CODE_ANALYSIS_ERROR and 3 FILE_NOT_FOUND, almost always as `&format!("{method} query failed: {error}")`.

WorkspaceQueryError::IncompleteSourceSnapshot is a retryable precondition failure - workspace_sources.rs even spells the retry advice into the GenerationChanged message - yet it reaches the client as the same INTERNAL_ERROR as a genuine bug, so no caller can distinguish retry from report.
The protocol already defines CODE_ANALYSIS_ERROR (-32000) and FILE_NOT_FOUND (-32001) for exactly this distinction (al-protocol/src/jsonrpc.rs:222-228).
detail.suggestion: Add one mapping function in daemon/mod.rs, `fn analysis_error_response(id: u64, method: &str, error: &dyn std::error::Error) -> Response`, and give the handful of query error enums that have a client-actionable case (WorkspaceQueryError, SourceLookupError, TestQueryError) a `fn rpc_code(&self) -> i32` returning CODE_ANALYSIS_ERROR or FILE_NOT_FOUND. Dispatchers then call the one mapper instead of hand-writing rpc_error(INTERNAL_ERROR, format!(...)), which removes text rather than adding a layer.

Nine files of 150+ LOC have no test at all, totalling 3,213 LOC: insight.rs 576, app/details.rs 507, views/event_chain.rs 425, app/mod.rs 380, cli/mod.rs 307, views/call_graph.rs 306, types.rs 254, cli/subcommands.rs 244, tui.rs 214.

app/details.rs::hydrate_selected_object is not presentation-only — it decides whether a slim symbol entry needs member hydration by checking six collections for emptiness, then replaces the entry in place and lazily opens a DaemonClient. A wrong emptiness check silently re-fetches on every keystroke or never fetches at all, and nothing would fail.

views/event_chain.rs and views/call_graph.rs are reached only by crates/al-explorer/src/lib.rs:234 event_chain_and_call_graph_queries_are_length_capped, which exercises input capping and nothing else; their render and data-fetch paths have no coverage.
detail.suggestion: Add inline #[cfg(test)] modules to app/details.rs and the two view modules covering the state transitions rather than the drawing: assert hydrate_selected_object issues one request for a slim entry and none for an already-hydrated one, and drive handle_event_chain_key / handle_call_graph_key through their state machines the way lib.rs:234 already does for input length. These need no terminal — they operate on App and the *View structs directly.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::tui_.summary: The only TUI test adapts its assertions to whichever daemon a prior test left resident

evidence: tui_smoke.rs:75 states the dependency outright: 'A fresh daemon labels the local package `(workspace)`, while a daemon reused by the full suite can expose it as `workspace`. Runtime sorts first in the latter case, so inspect the actual selection before moving.' The test then accepts either label and conditionally sends two arrow keys when '>> Runtime' is on screen.
The test does not call stop_project_daemon before spawning, so which branch runs depends on test execution order within the harness suite.

Its polling uses thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)) in a 15-iteration loop plus a 6-iteration loop, so a slow cold start costs up to ~42s of wall time and a slower one fails on a screen-content assertion that reports 'TUI may not have started'.
This single test is the whole TUI's coverage: it asserts three substrings ('Objects', a workspace package label, 'Source: workspace source').
detail.suggestion: Call al_test_harness::stop_project_daemon(&test_project_dir()) at the top of the test so it always measures a fresh daemon, then drop the dual-label branch and assert the single '(workspace)' label. Replace the 2s poll granularity with ~200ms against the same overall deadline so a fast daemon does not pay a 2s floor per check.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::daem.summary: stop_project_daemon documents a suite-wide hazard but is called in 1 of 23 harness test files

evidence: crates/al-test-harness/src/lib.rs:112-124 describes the hazard generally: 'The daemon is a per-project singleton that outlives the test that started it. Without this, a test whose result depends on how al-lsp was *built* ... silently measures whichever binary an earlier run happened to leave resident, so the same command passes or fails depending on working-tree history.'
Grep across crates/ finds exactly one call site: crates/al-test-harness/tests/semantic_bridge.rs:60.

cli_smoke.rs, tui_smoke.rs and mcp_stdio.rs all run al-explorer against the same bundled fixture at data/test_al_project and therefore share that singleton; cli_smoke.rs:442 already has to order `daemon-shutdown` last for the same reason.
cli_smoke.rs isolates XDG_CACHE_HOME/CONFIG_HOME/DATA_HOME per run and copies the project, showing the isolation pattern exists — it just is not applied to the daemon itself.
detail.suggestion: Call stop_project_daemon(&test_project_dir()) once at the start of each harness test file that spawns al-explorer against the shared fixture (cli_smoke, tui_smoke, mcp_stdio, extension_smoke), or have the auto-start path key the daemon on the isolated project copy these tests already create so no two files share one.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::ungu.summary: socket_path_is_deterministic sets XDG_RUNTIME_DIR process-wide with no restore and no serial guard

evidence: crates/al-lsp/src/server/daemon/mod.rs:1378 runs `std::env::set_var("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR", "/tmp")` and never restores it, so the value leaks to every later test in that binary.

The same crate already has the convention: crates/al-lsp/src/server/workspace.rs:2051/2061/2077 annotate their env-mutating tests with #[serial_test::serial], and al-lsp/Cargo.toml:98 carries serial_test as a dev-dependency.

daemon/mod.rs:95 calls socket_path(&project_root) in production, so any other test in the al-lsp lib binary that resolves a socket path now gets one derived from a forced /tmp runtime dir depending on thread scheduling.
Of 38 env-mutating tests in the workspace this and crates/al-protocol/src/socket.rs:191 are the only two unguarded, and the al-protocol one at least restores the previous value before asserting.
detail.suggestion: Add #[serial_test::serial] to socket_path_is_deterministic and restore the previous XDG_RUNTIME_DIR after the call, matching workspace.rs:2051. Better, call al_protocol::socket_path_with_runtime_dir(p, "/tmp") the way crates/al-protocol/src/socket.rs:210 does and mutate no environment at all.

completeness.rs:406 sleeps 500ms with the comment 'Give server a moment to process and publish cleared diagnostics' before asserting on drained diagnostics.
zed_simulation.rs:217 and real_world.rs:707 use the same pattern at 500ms and 200ms.

detail.suggestion: Replace each with the deadline loop already used at integration_full.rs:961 — poll drain_diagnostics every ~50ms until the expected state appears or a generous deadline (5s) expires, and assert on the drained value. For regression.rs:204 that also removes the hidden coupling to the server's debounce constant.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::alc_.summary: The emitter's byte-for-byte alc compatibility is guarded in CI only by a fixture with no drift check

evidence: emit_differential.rs:262/366/471 and pack_native_validate.rs:52/76 are all #[ignore] pending AL_TOOL_PATH and dotnet, and no job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `--ignored` or `make microsoft-contracts`.

In CI the claim therefore rests on crates/al-emit/src/symbol_reference_test.rs, whose header states the fixtures are 'real alc 17.0.34 output' and that they should be regenerated 'if the targeted toolchain changes' — an instruction with no automated check behind it.

The repository does enforce this kind of pin elsewhere: Docs/testing-guide.md documents `make check-record-methods`, which regenerates the Record method catalog and fails on DRIFT or PROVENANCE DRIFT. The emit fixtures have no equivalent.

crates/al-emit/src/symbol_extract.rs (1,190 LOC) and symbol_reference.rs (1,627 LOC) have no #[cfg(test)] module of their own and are reached only through symbol_reference_test.rs, so fixture staleness is their single point of failure.
detail.suggestion: Record the alc version the fixtures were generated from in crates/al-emit/src/testdata (a small version file) and assert it in symbol_reference_test.rs against the version `make microsoft-contracts` reports, so a toolchain pin move fails loudly instead of leaving the fixture silently describing an old compiler. Optionally add a scheduled workflow that runs `make microsoft-contracts` on a runner with the toolchain available.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::wall.summary: performance.rs asserts a 250ms wall-clock median for LSP queries in the default cargo test run

evidence: performance.rs:13 sets MAX_MEDIAN = 250ms and the measure! macro at :56 asserts the median of 7 samples is under it, for hover, completion, definition, document symbols and semantic tokens.
The test is not #[ignore]d, so it runs in `cargo test --workspace` on shared GitHub runners for both ubuntu-latest and macos-latest.

The file's own header argues it is 'intentionally an always-on hang/regression guard, not a shared-host microbenchmark or a cross-machine SLA', and .github/workflows/ci.yml keeps a separate Criterion bench for real timing — so the budget number is doing work the author explicitly does not want it to do.
Every other timing check in the suite is a deadline that only fails on a hang (cli_smoke.rs:49 uses 40s, integration_full.rs:960 uses 5s).
detail.suggestion: Raise MAX_MEDIAN to a hang-detection threshold in the seconds range (the stated intent) and keep the eprintln! timing report for humans, or gate the 250ms assertion behind an env var so only a controlled host enforces it. The per-operation success assertions inside each measure! block already cover correctness and should stay unconditional.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: One LSP query family encodes failure five different ways; find_implementations hides an unopened document as an empty result

evidence: Functions with the same (workspace, uri[, position]) signature return five different failure encodings: Vec<Location> (implementation.rs:16), Vec<SemanticToken> (semantic_tokens.rs:36), Option<Vec<AlFoldingRange>> (folding.rs:11), Option<Vec<AlDocumentSymbol>> (symbols.rs:12), Result<Vec<CodeLensEntry>, String> (code_lens.rs:81), Result<Option<Vec<AlInlayHint>>, String> (inlay_hints.rs:15), Result<Option<Vec<Location>>, WorkspaceStateError> (definition.rs:10).

implementation.rs:17-26 returns Vec::new() for all of: get_or_parse failing (document not open or unparseable), no node at the position, and node text not resolving to a clean name. The caller sees the same empty vector it would see for a real interface with no implementors.
folding.rs:12 and symbols.rs:13 use `?` on get_or_parse and return None for that identical condition, while definition.rs returns Err(WorkspaceStateError) for it.
detail.suggestion: Pick one encoding for the document-missing condition and apply it across the family. The cheapest coherent move: make find_implementations, semantic_tokens_full, folding_ranges and document_symbols return Result<Vec<_>, WorkspaceStateError> like definition/references/completions already do, so 'document not loaded' is an Err and an empty Vec means 'nothing found'. Convert code_lens and inlay_hints from String to the same typed error while touching them.

Option rather than Result because no error value exists at that point, only absence; the String-returning code_lens and inlay_hints belong to the al-analysis error-convention item.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: 39 public fallible functions return Result<_, String> next to siblings in the same module that use thiserror enums

evidence: profiler_hints.rs declares ProfilerHintError at line 43 and uses it for profiler_hints (line 291), but parse_profile (173), profile_hints_with_locations (360) and load_profile_file (595) in the same file return Result<_, String>. A caller handling profiler failures needs two error-handling styles inside one module.

Counting every public fallible function in crates/: 268 return Result, 229 with a typed error, 39 with String. 24 of the 39 are in al-analysis, whose other queries already define WorkspaceQueryError, AuditError, DuplicateError, ImpactError, SuggestEventError, TestQueryError and SourceLookupError.

All six public functions in bulk_fix.rs return Result<_, String>, as do native_check::id_ranges_from_app_json and affix_rules_from_appsourcecop, scaffold::create_project, and the whole DaemonClient surface in al-protocol/src/client.rs (connect, connect_existing, from_stream, request, request_with_timeout, find_al_lsp_binary).
String errors carry no variant a caller can match on, so downstream code either reformats the message or gives up on distinguishing failure modes.
detail.suggestion: Start with the modules that already have an error enum and finish the job: move parse_profile, profile_hints_with_locations and load_profile_file onto ProfilerHintError. Then add one thiserror enum per remaining module (BulkFixError for bulk_fix.rs, NativeCheckError for native_check.rs, DaemonClientError for al-protocol/src/client.rs) rather than a shared catch-all, so each module's failure modes stay named and matchable.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: The 85-method daemon JSON-RPC namespace mixes flat camelCase, dotted camelCase and dotted snake_case

evidence: The dispatch table at mod.rs:590-730 contains flat camelCase methods (documentSymbols, foldingRanges, semanticTokens, deadCode, tableImpact, traceChain, eventMap, insightStats, nativeCheck, downloadSymbols, newProject, errorCodes, builtinTypes, sortMembers, organizeFiles, eventSource, graphExport, sqlPatterns, clearCache), dotted namespaces with camelCase members (fix.applicationArea, fix.dataClassification, fix.tooltips, audit.dataClassification, deps.graph, arch.lint, profiler.hints, permissions.audit, xlf.generate, xlf.refresh, xlf.suggest, xlf.untranslated), and dotted namespaces with snake_case members (tests.run_batch, tests.run_auto, tests.last_results, tests.snapshot_validate, tests.snapshot_capture, tests.snapshot_replay, tests.snapshot_diff).
Flat and namespaced forms of the same noun both exist as separate methods: deps and deps.graph, permissions and permissions.audit, fix and fix.applicationArea, snapshot and tests.snapshot_capture.

This is the toolchain's external API — the CLI (al-explorer), the MCP server and the Zed extension all address it by method-name string, and al_call's description tells an agent to supply 'the daemon method name' with no way to derive it.
detail.suggestion: Settle on dotted namespace + camelCase member and rename the snake_case members (tests.runBatch, tests.runAuto, tests.lastResults, tests.snapshotCapture/Replay/Diff/Validate). Keep the existing spellings as aliases in the match arms for one release so the Zed extension and any pinned CLI keep working, and add the alias list to the daemon method reference so the rule is visible.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: Daemon methods split into two document-identifier conventions with nothing in the method name to signal which

evidence: extract_uri (mod.rs:852) reads only params['uri'] and is used by every lsp_dispatch handler (hover, definition, references, implementations, completions, signatureHelp, rename, documentSymbols, foldingRanges, semanticTokens, inlayHints, codeActions).

file_uri_from_params (mod.rs:1123) accepts 'uri' OR 'file', rejects both-present, resolves a relative 'file' against the process cwd and canonicalises it. It is used by fixes.rs (4 call sites), build/metrics.rs and build/organize.rs.
A client calling `metrics` with 'uri' and `hover` with 'file' gets opposite outcomes, and the method names give no hint which convention applies.

review::.::holistic::authorization_consi.summary: env-token-then-OAuth precedence is copy-pasted at four dispatch sites; only bc_server recovers from a 401

evidence: debug_dispatch.rs:306-334, tests_dispatch.rs:2074-2103 and al-lsp.rs:339-350 each spell out the same sequence by hand: access_token_from_env() -> Some means use it, None means build a fresh reqwest::Client and call oauth::acquire_token, with per-site error mapping.

detail.suggestion: Add one async resolver next to access_token_from_env in crates/al-bc/src/http_auth.rs (or a small al-symbols::oauth::resolve_token(tenant) wrapper) that owns the env -> cached -> interactive precedence and the 401 invalidation hook, then have debug_dispatch.rs, tests_dispatch.rs, al-lsp.rs and bc_server.rs::add_auth all call it instead of restating the sequence.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::untype.summary: The 84-method daemon protocol has no derived types in either direction, so every payload shape is restated by hand three times

evidence: Zero Deserialize derives across roughly 90 daemon methods; 131 hand-rolled extract_* calls against 5 serde_json::from_value
The client side reads responses with about 504 raw .get("field") calls against 2 from_value sites
response_contract.rs is 1451 hand-maintained lines validating 60 of 84 methods at runtime
The same payload contract is therefore stated in the daemon's extractors, the contract validator and the MCP JSON schemas, with nothing keeping the three in step
detail.suggestion: Define a #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] struct per method in the shared al-protocol crate and use it on both sides. The compiler then enforces what response_contract.rs checks at runtime, so that file mostly goes away: this removes roughly 1500 lines rather than adding a layer.
